headline: Harvard Law School has expanded its CPT cutoff to all 13 externship clinics (previously only some), and says it is individually advising students already enrolled in those clinics about alternatives — the most direct look yet at a major program handling students mid-placement, though it stops short of an explicit stop-work order, so Harvard stays in the posture-not-stated tier. No school moved tier this run; Davidson, MIT, Skidmore and the University of South Florida remain the only schools confirmed to have interrupted already-granted CPT.

tripwires.name: DHS SEVIS Help Hub CPT page
tripwires.detail: Direct fetch succeeded again 7 Oct 00:17 UTC (7 Oct 08:17 HKT). Page unchanged, still "Last Updated: August 24, 2026," same BCM 2608-01/2608-02 references; cancellation section still only states a DSO can cancel CPT before its start date and, after the start date, can only edit the authorisation to shorten the end date — not cancel it outright. No change to the page itself.

tripwires.name: Tufts I-Center CPT page
tripwires.detail: Direct fetch succeeded again 7 Oct 00:17 UTC — the "due to recent updates to guidelines, the I-Center is unable to process CPT requests for non-required internships at this time" sentence is still present, unchanged; still nothing either way about students who already hold CPT authorisation. No change detected.

tripwires.name: Federal Register rulemaking on CPT
tripwires.detail: Checked 7 Oct 00:17 UTC — no CPT-specific NPRM published, underlying CPT regulation (8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(i)) not amended; DHS's own CPT-guidance tripwire page still says SEVP 'plans to release draft guidance' clarifying prior CPT documents, no date given. CPT remains guidance (12/24 Aug broadcast messages), not a rule.

tripwires.name: Retroactive cancellation spreading
tripwires.detail: Still tripped, re-checked 7 Oct 00:17 UTC — no school newly moved into 'cancels' this run. Closest watch item remains Harvard Law School, per the Harvard Crimson (5 Oct): ended CPT for all 13 externship clinics (previously only some) and is individually advising students already enrolled in those clinics about alternatives — concerning but not an explicit stop-work/revocation statement, so Harvard stays 'unstated.' Davidson, MIT, Skidmore and University of South Florida remain the only confirmed interruptions of already-granted CPT.

context: No CPT-specific litigation. No third broadcast message. DHS's stated position: 'nothing about these regulations has changed.' ICE is auditing schools, with SEVP decertification as the stated risk. Immigration attorneys flag a retroactive-scrutiny risk — past CPT revisited at the OPT, STEM-OPT or H-1B stage. The common institutional reading of the new standard: integral to the curriculum, required of all students in the programme for degree completion, a documented cooperative agreement with the employer, and DSO authorisation before training begins.
